dedupe_keys.name: sub saharan africa high resolution electrification grids

description: Mendeley Data hosts high-resolution electrification estimates for sub-Saharan Africa. The own page lists NetCDF outputs for the number of people without electricity access in each grid cell between 2014 and 2020 and for estimated consumption tier in electrified cells in 2018. A text file points to a finer Google Earth Engine version. The grids can help locate unmet demand or test where an electrification model places new connections. They are estimates based on settlement and other source layers, not meter records for individual households. The Mendeley page shows version 6 and notes that version 4 changed the licence to CC BY 4.0; DataCite also lists CC BY 4.0. I read the article and own repository metadata without obtaining the grids or using Earth Engine. The linked preparation code is a separate G1 item. No exact catalogue coverage was found. A caveat is that inferred access grids can understate local connection quality. They support infrastructure capacity planning when used as model inputs, but do not report feeder performance.
